I really enjoy Hidden Object games, and considering this is one based in fairy tales (or the Slavic equivalent), I was super excited to play.  This is the first in the Eventide Trilogy.

You play as a famous botanist who is on her way to a park she had spent a lot of time in growing up that is owned and run by her grandmother.  While on her way, she is run off of the road by a very large bat-like creature, and is subsequently rescued by Boruta.  Come to find out, Boruta and the bat creature are working together and they manage to kidnap your grandma!  From here, you work with the mysterious park inhabitants to get to stop Boruta and save your grandma!

The storyline itself is captivating and easy to follow, making it a lovely game for people of all ages to enjoy.  Considering other Artifex Mundi games I have played in the past, this game did seem overly simplified and the story wasn't as in-depth or as rich.  There is a lot of potential that could have gone into the storyline on the origin of the creatures, how the park came to be, and could have included more of the creature interactions themselves.  Despite that, the game is still good enough that it's enjoyable to play.  The map is split into two sections instead of multiple chapters, which makes it really easy to backtrack between scenes for different items or interactions.  Now, icons on the map can be related to one or two different scenes, so there still can be a little confusion, but the game is simple enough it's easy to figure out what is where.  The characters are enjoyable to meet and interact with (though I wish I could interact with more of the characters from the beginning) and the designs were creative.  The game itself is fairly short, and can easily be completed in around 5 hours, though that easily is doubled if you achievement hunt and play the bonus content.

Just like most of Artifex Mundi's games, the artwork and designs of the scenery and the characters is breathtaking and is clearly a labor of love.  Every scene is whimsical and beautiful, taking advantage of the lighting of fire or moonlight to add depth.  Despite some areas being more broken down than before, it still felt very touristy, and I loved seeing the details in every moment.

With this being a hidden-object game, there weren't a whole lot of those.  There were more puzzles in this than hidden objects, but I did appreciate the variety that were given.  Some of the HO games were word-based, others were picture based.  Some even had one particular item you had to find multiple of.  The HO games didn't seem repetitive and were spread out with multiple kinds of puzzles, which made it so much more engaging.  
To add to that, there are two different kinds of collectibles you can find throughout the game~  You have creature cards (think Pokemon cards, but with Slavic fairy tale creatures) and you have flowers!  The creature cards had descriptions to them, and I was so excited to see what the next one was!  I just wish there were more of those creatures added into the game itself.

The achievements you can get in the game are kind of standard for most HO games with there being story-based ones, then achievements linked to the puzzles and HO games you play, and others linked to the collectibles.  There is always a variety, but if you play a lot of Artifex Mundi's games, you know what to expect for most of them.  Still very achievable and can easily be gotten within a couple playthroughs!  

Overall, I do recommend playing this game.  It is a wonderful starting place for those that don't play a lot of these or want to introduce them to their kids since it is very simple.  While the game itself wasn't one of the greatest HO games I've played, it certainly held its own.  It's short, simple, and sweet, and definitely is worth it's price point.  I can't wait to play the other games in the series to see how they compare!

[b]Eventide: Slavic Fable[/b] is first game of the Eventide series published by Artifex Mundi, following with Eventide 2: The Sorcerers Mirror and Eventide 3: Legacy of Legends. It's a point & click mystery adventure hidden object game. It's loosely based on slavic folklore creatures and mythology. 

[b]Plot summary[/b]  - Your name is Mary Gilbert and you work as endangered species savior or botanist what would you call it. You get a letter from your dear grandma 'baba', who is asking you to save the endangered flower that keeps the whole Moorland village alive, but this turns out to be least of your concern. You meet with a man named Boruta, who seems nice and helpful at first. Turns out they aren't what they claimed to be and they are just a maniac who wants power over humans and eternal life. You are helped by mythical creatures of the forest who are friends with your grandma and for in return you promise to provide them with the magical powder that makes them human again. Boruta kidnaps your grandma to use them as human sacrifice in their midnight ritual, you need to save them and the forest before it's too late. 

[b]Extra chapter[/b] plot doesn't have anything to do with the main story, it has same characters and places, but no indications to the main game story. You are small girl, i assume it's Mary's mother in this story, but not completely sure if i caught any names that indicate that. They live with their mother - Baba/grandma from the main story. Mother is sick and little girl wants to save her, for that they need the endangered pink mythical flower. You escape from the house in the night and travel to the forest where you have to help creatures to prove you have pure heart, that is needed to get to the flower. 

My personal opinion about the plot is that it's nothing special. I like to play more of the realistic stories that are taking place in modern/modernish times, but this wasn't so bad. Plot is your typical one you see in these games. I have started to notice that almost all or at least good amount of Artifex Mundi games follow the exact same plot line. You have the main character who is helped by a person at first, they turn out to be the evil bad guy and then you have to chase them down and make world a better place again. I'm amused how often the evil in the game first are seen as the helping good guy. Even though the plot was cookie cutter same as in others, i think it was decently executed in this one so it wasn't extremely boring. 

[b]Mechanics and game play[/b] of the game were good. You don't have map in the first part of the game, but you obtain it quite early which makes the in game moving easier. Gotta point out minor oddity in this game, map is 2 sided and you need to flip it, haven't seen that before. You have your basic journal, where you can see your notes and stories you have found. You have [b]three (3) difficulty levels[/b], i played this on expert even though i usually like to play on advanced, but that choice was only because the one achievement you can get, i'll explain it later in the review. 

[b]There was plenty of HO scenes[/b], few of them were repetitive, but that isn't  a problem if it only stays in a few. I think over half of the HO's were find by shape ones, instead find by the word/names. I like the name ones more personally, but i think overall in this game there's a good balance in the HO's. You have extra chapter after the main story, which is always a plus in my books. I have played so many of these type of games so far that almost every game seems to be same kind, that is where i come to the mini games. They are same, same ones i have played hundred times across the genre. There wasn't any rare or special mini game that you don't see often, because all of them were the sames that you see often, specially in Artifex Mundi games. I ain't game developer just a gamer, but i think that there should be many new options for the mini games in the world or am i wrong? Something new and refreshing would be cool, because at the moment it's just that i know how they work, what is the logic behind the puzzles to solve them, so it's just me brainless clicking the puzzle in less than few minutes to solve it. Also what comes to the puzzles in this game, some of the so claimed 'puzzles' didn't even feel like ones, they were more like interactive stories. Too easy for to even be called puzzle, you just place the symbols/pictures over the obvious spots while there is story telling. 

You can also find extra materials in the main menu, like music, wallpapers, mini games and so on. That is always a plus in my opinion. I liked the art work, but Artifex Mundi rarely disappoints in that category to be honest. It gave me a children's book dreamy magical forest vibes. Music was fitting and good, didn't feel repetitive. Voice acting was between decent and good. I don't have my hopes up what comes to the acting in these types of games, but in this one i think it was OK.

[b]Achievements[/b] were good in my opinion. Only achievement i didn't like was the complete the game in hard difficulty. When it might not be a problem for me to play the game on hard, i think it leaves out some players, specially the ones who haven't played these games much and want to get some help in the game. These type of games are usually played pass time like in a light casual way. There are missable achievements like the collect all cards one and there isn't clear indicator that there is card seen on the scene like some games do, but i would say overall still it's kinda hard to miss the cards or flowers for example since often they aren't so well hidden. Most of the achievements come with the story as you go, few of them are based on the mini games and HO scenes, like find all objects in less than minute etc. I got all the achievements quite easily. Even if you miss one flower like for example in the first part of the game, you can go back there almost always since there isn't really blocked places. 

What comes to the [b]game length[/b], it didn't take me so long to play little bit over 3 hours on hard adding the extra chapter, played on pc. I would say for someone not so familiar of this genre, maybe 5 hours or so. It's not that long and that is what is considered in my next statement. This game is 14,79 euros (16,09 USD) without sale, i would not recommend this unless it's on a sale. Personally i can't justify myself buying a game with that price when i only get few hours of play from it and probably never going to play again. I would wait it to come to a like over 50% sale.

Pros
• Extra chapter.
• Plot is decent.
• Extra material in main menu.
• Good amount of HO's.
• Plenty of mini games.
• 3 difficulty levels.
• You can get achievements in one game play.
• Great for people who are new to these type of games or want casual chill game to play.

Cons
• Most of the puzzles are way too easy, same ones that you see in other games. Some of them i wouldn't even call puzzles.
• High price, unless in sale.
• No indicator if there is collectible present.
• You have to play the game on hard to get all the achievements.

My first Artifex Mundi game! 

I chose this as my entrance because I love witchy botanical vibes, which it very much delivered on!

I didn't know anything really about Slavic mythology before going into this game so it was really interesting  delving into that for me. 

The puzzles were fun, a lot of hidden object puzzles as you'd expect, but also a few different types of puzzles- a few of which I got stuck on for a while! You can choose which difficulty you'd like at the start of the game - casual, advanced, or expert. I chose casual as I wasn't sure what to expect with this being my first Artifex Mundi game. I intend to go back and play the game on Expert to get the achievement and to see how it weighs against casual.

The cutscenes are....... hilarious. The animations are just so bad, but so bad that they're good again. But the static graphics are really pretty. The game gives you them as wallpapers too which is pretty neat! There's also some bonus content including a bonus adventure. This was a nice little story that revisted some of the locations with slight differences.

I streamed my playthrough to some friends so it became more of a group activity, which I very much recommend! It added more levels of fun and a touch of competition.

Overall, I definitely recommend this and will be going on to play the next games in the series!
